summary: Steel fire tower on a hill at Ardbeg, Parry Sound District; E.R. Nesbitt manned it from 1928 to 1938 and it was staffed until the early 1970s. No source says what remains.

facts.agency: Ontario Department of Lands and Forests

events.note: E.R. Nesbitt is recorded as manning the tower from 1928 to 1938.
Listed on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map (1963), per Firelookout.ca.

evidence.supports: Tower stood on a small hill where the road meets the railway
evidence.quote: It stood on a small hill where the road meets the railway.

evidence.supports: Ardbeg is a community of the Municipality of Whitestone
evidence.quote: The municipality comprises the communities of: Ardbeg

evidence.supports: Municipality of Whitestone formed in 2000 from unorganized Parry Sound District land
evidence.quote: In 2000, the Municipality of Whitestone was formed out of Unorganized Centre Parry Sound District

Lou was assisted by four other men
evidence.quote: helped to build this tower, and was assisted by Claude Bosley, M. Bosley, Harry Blacksky and John Musquaty.

evidence.quote: The materials were brought to the site using Nesbitt’s team of horses.

evidence.supports: E.R. Nesbitt manned the tower 1928 to 1938
evidence.quote: Tower was manned by E.R. Nesbitt from 1928 - 1938.

evidence.quote: Appears on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map (1963).

evidence.quote: They came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

evidence.supports: Staffed until the early 1970s when aerial detection took over
evidence.quote: which was one of the last remaining staffed fire towers in Southern Ontario until the early 1970s when aerial forest fire detection took over.

evidence.supports: Wikipedia describes the tower in the past tense as once a popular attraction
evidence.quote: A popular attraction was once the Ardbeg fire tower

notes_for_editor: Two web sources plus one Firelookout.ca record, which is the only Ardbeg-specific source; its notes credit Murray Woods. The record's Year Built field is blank, so the story gives no build year and the events list has no built event. Height is not recorded (height_m omitted); the 261 m figure is elevation, not structure height. Wikipedia uses the past tense and gives no removal date or site status, so the fate is unconfirmed. An Ominous listing titled 'Ardbeg Fire Tower - Historic Location Foundations' appeared only as a search snippet; the fetched Ominous page was a sign-in screen, so the foundations claim is not used. Geocache GC33MD4 and the fire-department wiki (HTTP 403) gave nothing usable. The 1928-1938 Nesbitt tenure and the early-1970s end of staffing describe different periods and do not conflict. Access is unknown and is left out of facts.
